entities.summary: Billy Russell Kinard was an American football player and coach. He played professionally as a defensive back for the Cleveland Browns and Green Bay Packers of the National Football League (NFL) and the Buffalo Bills of the American Football League (AFL). Kinard played college football at the University of Mississippi before being drafted by the Cleveland Browns in the second round of the 1956 NFL draft. He played professionally for four seasons and retired in 1960. Kinard later served as the head football coach at Ole Miss from 1971 to 1973 and at Gardner–Webb University in 1978, compiling a career coaching record of 20–14–1.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Billy Kinard's coaching career at Ole Miss and Gardner–Webb University had a significant impact on Southern college football in the 1970s, with his teams compiling a record of 20–14–1. His tenure as head coach at Ole Miss helped shape the program into a consistent regional power.
